questions.stem: For Brightwater Foods, a startup firm, a perceptual map of the Marovia market plots brands on price (budget to premium) and service level (low to high). Most competitors cluster in the premium, high service corner, leaving the opposite corner empty. What does the empty corner suggest for the firm?
questions.explanation: A perceptual map shows how brands are positioned in customers' minds on key dimensions. A cluster of competitors in one corner with an empty opposite corner suggests a possible gap, a position few brands occupy, which could be an opportunity if enough buyers want it. An empty spot does not prove there is no demand; it may mean the combination has simply not been offered. The map is a tool for spotting exactly this kind of opening.
questions.hint: Read the empty space as a possible gap, not as proof of no demand.
questions.learningObjective: read a perceptual map for positioning gaps

options.text: The empty corner proves no customer wants those attributes
options.misconception: mistakes an empty position for absent demand

options.text: The budget, low service position may be an underserved positioning opportunity
Perceptual maps cannot show gaps in the market
options.misconception: denies the map's main diagnostic purpose

options.text: The firm should copy the crowded corner exactly
options.misconception: ignores the strategic value of differentiation

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Redstone Mattresses, a small firm drafts: "For busy parents in Yewton who need quick weeknight meals, our brand is the convenient meal kit that delivers fresh ingredients fast, unlike frozen dinners that taste bland." Which element is missing from this otherwise complete positioning statement?
questions.explanation: A strong positioning statement identifies the target market, the customer need, the brand's benefit and a point of difference from alternatives. This draft covers busy parents, their need for quick meals, the benefit of fresh ingredients delivered fast, and contrasts with bland frozen dinners. Price, a full competitor list and a media plan are not required elements of the statement itself, so nothing essential is missing.
questions.hint: List the standard parts of a positioning statement and check each one.
questions.learningObjective: evaluate the parts of a positioning statement

options.text: A specific price point for the product
options.misconception: treats price as a mandatory element of a positioning statement

options.text: The name of every competing brand
options.misconception: confuses a point of difference with a full competitor list

options.text: A detailed media plan for the campaign
options.misconception: mixes positioning with implementation planning

options.text: Nothing essential is missing; it states target, need, benefit and point of difference

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Foxglove Mattresses, a fast-growing firm sells 6 distinct product lines in Mapleridge, and each line carries 9 different items. What is the total number of items in the product mix?
questions.explanation: The total number of items, the depth of the whole mix, is the number of product lines multiplied by the number of items in each line: 6 times 9 equals 54. Adding the two figures would mix a count of lines with a count of per-line items, and quoting either number alone captures only part of the mix.
questions.hint: Each line holds several items, so multiply.

options.misconception: counts only the product lines
adds lines and depth instead of multiplying them
counts only the items in one line
